findings.title: Theme guard's comment stripper treats `/*` inside string literals as a comment opener, hiding real code up to the next `*/`
.dockerignore/.gitignore mirror test compares lines literally, but Docker anchors patterns at the context root while git matches at any depth

The .dockerignore mirror test compares pattern strings, but Docker anchors patterns to the context root, so files git ignores in subdirectories still reach the image while the smoke evidence reports a clean commit
The theme guard's block-comment stripper starts at `/*` inside an ordinary string literal (e.g. `accept="image/*"`) and deletes all code up to the next `*/`
Theme guard misses ordinary camelCase or underscored scheme class names ('darkMode', 'isDark', 'lightTheme', 'mode_dark')

.dockerignore 'mirror' matches .gitignore by string only: Docker anchors patterns at the context root, git does not, so nested git-ignored files (public/uploads/, src/**/*.log, …) reach the image while the smoke reports a clean commit
Scheme-word invariant misses ordinary camelCase class names ('darkMode', 'isLight', 'appDark')
.dockerignore 'mirror' test compares text, but Docker anchors patterns at the root, so files git ignores in subfolders still reach the image
